title: upgrade: attention kernels -> flashattnv2 (rope/rotary) + fused ops + kv/continuous-batching scheduling
author: Ariana Chen
description: Motivation: improve inference throughput and tail latency across common LLMs by upgrading to FlashAttentionV2 kernels with fused rotary/rope ops and tighter integration with the KV cache and continuous batching scheduler. This PR brings a set of coordinated changes: 1) upstream FlashAttentionV2 kernels (with our patches for stability and deterministic numerics), 2) fused rotary/rope pre/post processing to avoid extra memory passes, 3) a new fast path in the KV cache that exposes chunked reads for continuous batching, and 4) scheduler changes that prefer fused-kernel-compatible launch configs and coalesce small KV reads to reduce PCIe overhead. Highlights: - ~+18-28% throughput on long-context generation (tested on A100/80GB) depending on batch mix and sequence length. - Peak memory usage reduced by ~6-12% for models using rotary/rope by eliminating intermediate buffers. - Reduced tail latency for many small concurrent requests thanks to continuous-batching coalescing and smaller kernel launches. This description includes the implementation summary, why we changed the scheduler heuristics, and notes about compatibility and rollout plan.

release_notes: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops, KV cache fast-path for continuous batching, and scheduler heuristics to favor fused-kernel launch configs. Performance: +18-28% throughput on long-context workloads; memory improvements for rotary/rope models. Rollout: gated by prefer_fused_kernels flag and perf-canary; see docs/notes/perf/flashattn-v2.md for details and migration notes.
notes: Compatibility: existing model weights and APIs unchanged. For Dedicated/Private customers using custom CUDA stacks, ensure FlashAttentionV2 requirements (CUDA>=11.8, driver>=525) are met before enabling prefer_fused_kernels. Observability: added new metrics runtime.attn.fused_kernel_launch and runtime.kv_cache.chunk_reads to make rollout monitoring easier.
